chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave who marries a free woman and is later emancipated, then commits an immoral act: He said, 'There is no stoning upon him until he engages in intercourse with the free woman after his emancipation.' I asked, 'Does the free woman have the option (to annul the marriage) when he is freed?' He said, 'No, for her? He said, 'No, for she accepted him while he was a slave, and he remains upon his original marriage.'

key_terms.الْحُرَّةَ: Free woman (as opposed to a slave woman)
key_terms.الْخِيَارُ: Option/choice (specifically the right to annul the marriage)
key_terms.فَاحِشَةً: Immoral act (often referring to minor adultery or fornication not requiring stoning)

ai.seo_question: What happens to the marriage of a slave who marries a free woman if he is later freed?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this ruling to clarify that emancipation does not automatically dissolve the marriage between a slave and a free woman, as she accepted his status at the time of the contract. The Imam specifies that the husband is not subject to stoning (Rajm) for adultery until he commits the act after his full emancipation, highlighting the legal distinction between the slave's and free man's penal status. This establishes the principle of continuity in marital bonds despite changes in the husband's social rank, provided the wife consents to the initial union.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5029 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who reported from Abu Abdullah (as) regarding a slave who marries a free woman and is later emancipated but then commits an immoral act.

Imam (as) said: "There is no stoning (rajm) upon him until he engages in intercourse with the free woman after his emancipation."
I asked: "Does the free woman have the option (to leave him) when he is freed?"
Imam (as) replied: "No, for she accepted him while he was a slave, and he remains upon his original marriage."
